content.summary: Exact arithmetic and degenerate-case checks confirm the integer rounding, closed-neighborhood correction, nonempty H2 choice and final graph-fiber cap. The inequalities alone permit m=40 at q=9, so the manuscript appropriately concludes eighty without promoting the stronger45 diagnostic. No correction is required.

checks.method: Run scratch/alpha/round05_arithmetic.py to enumerate all integral q in 0..12 and m in 0..99 satisfying the two displayed inequalities; check the exact elimination arithmetic. Larger m are already excluded by 2m≤9q≤108.
checks.observation: The maximum feasible m is40, attained numerically only at q=9. The displayed cancellation gives37m≤1512 and floor(1512/37)=40, with37·41=1517. Empty overlap correctly forces m=0. This verifies the bound and shows that these incidence inequalities do not establish cap45 or attainability of any family.

checks.scope: Profile A rounding, nonempty choice and graph fibers
checks.method: Independently evaluate the closed-neighborhood bounds, enumerate nonnegative census solutions, and enumerate all64 simple graphs on four outsider points in scratch/alpha/round05_arithmetic.py.
checks.observation: The +2 correction gives meeting caps57 and52 and hence nine disjoint completions for an H2 row. Before using that row, the census already forces n2≥15, so its selection is noncircular. Adding n0≥9 leaves exactly(9,28,24),(10,26,25),(11,24,26),(12,22,27) for(n0,n1,n2). Every four-vertex graph with maximum degree≤2 has at most four edges; combining five keys with this cap gives20<24.
